newsitem.title: FRANCE: Swissair cargo hit by French strike.
newsitem.headline: Swissair cargo hit by French strike.

text.p: Swissair's cargo activities at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airport have been brought to a near-standstill today as a result of strike action by staff protesting at plans to cut jobs.

"Since early this morning there has no been no freight leaving from or arriving at Swissair installations at CDG, with the exception of some valuables shipments which were transported on passenger flights," a CDG-based Swissair cargo official told Reuters.
There was very little cargo blocked in Swissair's CDG warehouse as the airline had made contingency plans for shipments before the strike began, notably for perishables, the official said.
Swissair normally operates three trucking rotations daily between Paris and Zurich, Geneva and Basle," but these services had been suspended today, the official added
"We don't expect the situation to change for the remainder of today and we should know by late afternoon whether the strike will continue into tomorrow,"
The dispute centres on Swissair's French restructuring programme which involves cutting 66 jobs, including around 25 staff in cargo handling operations, which will be outsourced from January 1 1997.
Swissair's passenger flights from Paris to Zurich, Geneva and Basle, are operating normally, an airline official said.
